title: Boyhood sports and boxing lessons with Kid Carter
summary: Hurdles, broad jump and dash, and a neighbourhood former champion who taught the kids boxing.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: As a youth, what other interests did you have besides music?
I was always into sports. I was a pretty good hurdler, and I was a broad jumper and a dash man.
Somewhere I read something about your – some interest in boxing . . .
and a gentleman named Kid Carter.

Kid Carter was the gentleman in the neighborhood who used to gather up all of us kids and teach us the manly art of self defense. He taught it to us the hard way. He’d walked up to you and punch you in the belly. Bam. “Get that – suck that belly in. Tighten up them muscles.” He gave us all a very good understanding about the art of self defense. He was a great guy. He was a former champion in St. Louis. I don’t remember what weight, whether it was lightweight, middle, featherweight, or welter, whatever. But he was a very good boxer. Good cat. In my book, [?]’s got a whole chapter on that.
Oh yeah. I was pretty good. Archie Moore once said – the man said, “If you stayed involved in boxing, you would have been the champion.” That’s what Archie said. I was pretty good at it.
